candidates.title: Cap verifier search and vote among top-ranked samples
candidates.rule: When reranking with a learned verifier, do not scale candidate count indefinitely: around 400 completions accuracy peaked and then declined; and instead of taking only the top-1, majority-vote over the final answers of the top few (3-5 of 100 samples, ~30 of 3200).
candidates.passage: performance improves as we increase the number of completions up to 400. Beyond this point, performance start to decrease.
candidates.finding: With a 6B verifier on GSM8K, more candidates helped only up to roughly 400, after which adversarial solutions that fool the verifier reduced accuracy. Majority voting over top-ranked samples improved over top-1 selection, with the optimal vote pool growing with the number of samples drawn.
candidates.conditions: Verifiers trained on 100 completions per training problem; test-time search over larger pools; voting counts only final answers.
candidates.limitations: The 400 turnover point was measured only at 6B on GSM8K and may shift with verifier size, verifier quality, or task; exact accuracies not reported in text; single run details unclear.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep candidate counts (10, 100, 400, 1600) and vote-pool sizes on your task and verifier, plotting accuracy to find your own saturation point before fixing a budget.

reason: The paper runs controlled comparisons on GSM8K with GPT-3 6B/175B covering sample-and-rank verification vs finetuning, test-time sample count and voting, and verifier design ablations. These support several scoped, actionable rules; I avoid turning the dataset description or scaling extrapolations into rules.
